manual_notes: First-party release-header selection and ten-row pagination are implemented; assigned plugin rows and failed-to-CRITICAL normalization are supported by code and tests. Full stable-provenance/freshness acceptance remains unverified: assignment-created details include package/assignment IDs, but status upsert constructs details:nil and the resource upserts that field. No end-to-end evidence traced preservation of those details or stale/unknown classification in /services.
rationale: Substantial shared-task delivery covers pagination and ordinary status publication, but the exact selected provenance and freshness requirements need further verification. Do not convert this uncertainty into a negative abandonment label.

sources.observed_facts: Inspected assignment service registration, failure normalization in Go push loop, and regression assertions for pending service rows, provenance metadata and failed status mapping.
Pinned UI has a release selector in the First-party Repository Plugins header and paginates selected catalog rows with page size ten.
Assignment creation sets assignment_id, plugin_id, package_id and package_version in details. build_attrs_from_status sets details:nil and reduces incoming message to its summary.
The upsert action includes details in upsert_fields, so preservation of assignment-created provenance across status updates is not established by this path.

limitations: Static source/test review only; no tests, benchmarks, deployments or production systems were run.
Evidence uses recovered public GitHub path-history commits. Their equivalence to the original dataset revision is not asserted; no completion date is inferred from the last specification edit.
review_depth: Read full selected specification/shared tasks; inspected actual pagination component, full service registry, resource upsert fields, agent normalization/status construction and relevant assertion-based tests. Stale/freshness UI semantics were not verified end to end.
